detail: The parish conservation survey documents gray-blue ashlar, granite plinth, two slate roof pitches, the copper flèche shifted west, the lower west choir, south sacristy, pointed tracery and two portals in the east gable.
The government property steward gives the church’s approximate overall 70 by 35 m envelope and the origins of the double monastery.
The management account identifies former Folkung palace masonry, the brick northern range, rendered western range, 1956–1969 conservation and current museum and hotel uses.
The former Brothers’ Convent acquired its present body in 1763–1770 from Carl Johan Cronstedt’s alterations. Its later hospital use and preservation establish the standing era.
The site steward identifies the standing church and ranges and the low fragmentary ruin park between the brothers’ and sisters’ precincts.
